criteria.evidence: Independent bwrap rerun completed 7/7 unittest cases with exit code 0; fixture was mounted read-only and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

Independent bwrap rerun completed 4/4 acceptance cases with exit code 0 using guest_worker.py and output confined to guest tmpfs. Historical round-1 probe exit 1 reproduces the seeded punctuation defect; historical round-2 probe exit 0 verifies correction.

Read-only SQLite inspection observed 15 unique events in order: TASK_HANDOFF, RORCH_EXECUTING, SELF_TEST, SUBMITTED_FOR_QA, QA_RUNNING, QA_REJECTED, REWORK_REQUIRED, RORCH_EXECUTING, SELF_TEST, SUBMITTED_FOR_QA, QA_RUNNING, QA_PASS, MORCH_REVIEW, ACCEPTED, TERMINAL_COMPLETED.
The ledger and actor artifacts correlate QA_REJECTED to RORCH_FIX and a second QA_PASS; qa_probe_round1.json and qa_probe_round2.json contain reproducible before/after results.
Seven completed stages have seven distinct Hermes session IDs, with separate MORCH, RORCH and QA stage directories and supervisor-spawn transport labels. This is process/session separation only.

QA used separate sessions and a deterministic probe but the same Hermes installation, provider=custom and model=20261030_RORCH as MORCH/RORCH. The supervisor supplies actor labels and verdict-directed prompts; no independently authenticated transport principal or separate permission boundary was demonstrated.

SQLite contains 4 messages, all direction=OUTBOX and already status=ACKED; INBOX count is 0. send_message inserts ACKED and acked_at in the same transaction. No receiver claim, inbox consumer, independent ACK/NACK, retry worker or ambiguous-send reconciliation is evidenced.

15/15 event IDs and event idempotency keys are unique; 4/4 message idempotency keys are unique. A later regeneration of functional_result.json left the SQLite database at the same 15 events and 4 messages, providing bounded terminal-rerun evidence.

run_phase1_resume_stdout.log records a controlled stop after QA_REJECTED; run_phase2_stdout.log reaches TERMINAL_COMPLETED. Final ledger has one QA_REJECTED, one REWORK_REQUIRED, one QA_PASS and no duplicate keys. This proves bounded supervisor restart recovery, not lease-expiry or crash-during-commit recovery.

After supervisor launch, stage transitions and actor handoffs were generated by the supervisor without manual message transfer; actor results report human_relay_count=0 and the ledger contains the automatic edges MORCH->RORCH, QA->RORCH, QA->MORCH and MORCH->RORCH.
Actor and transport identities are supervisor-provided strings. No cryptographic or platform-authenticated sender binding is verified before FSM transitions or ACK state.
All seven stages used provider=custom and model=20261030_RORCH. No second model/provider or fallback execution is present.

reproduction.command_summary: bwrap network/user namespace isolation; fixture ro-bind; python3 -B -m unittest -v test_app.py
bwrap network/user namespace isolation; fixture ro-bind; guest_worker.py qa-probe /tmp/qa.json

reproduction.result: 15 events, 4 messages, 7 stages; no duplicate keys

limitations: This review is NTV_FUNCTIONAL only and does not certify NTV_ROOT, protected-root hygiene, rollback, ACLs, mounts, child-process writes, or post-close drift.
The real functional QA probe is distinct from full independent QA authority: it verifies behavior, while identity and permission independence remain unverified.
The overall FAIL is caused by missing inbox/receiver ACK semantics and unauthenticated actor origin, not by application behavior.
No live Slack or GitHub transport was exercised by this fixture review.
Costs are reported by Hermes as unknown/zero-estimate and were not independently priced.
